Wait, but looking at this more carefully: 101/756 at 00:56 and 102/756 at 01:30. So the delta is 34 seconds for one step (101→102). That's about 34s/step actual step time. But the tqdm speed says 1.02s/it which is the average. 

The average is being skewed by the initial checkpoint loading that got skipped from step 0 to 100. Looking at the progression more carefully, the elapsed time jumped from 00:56 to 01:30 — that's 34 seconds for just step 102. So the actual per-step time is around 34s, which is still pretty slow. Though I should remember this is GRPO with gradient_accumulation_steps=16, so each step is processing 64 completions total (16 mini-batches × 4 generations per sample). That might actually be reasonable performance.

Comparing to the original r3 baseline which ran at ~100s/step on CPU NLI, getting 34s/step with GPU NLI is about a 3x speedup. But the target was supposed to be around 12s/step, so there's still room for improvement. Let me look for more data points to understand what's happening.

Actually, I'm realizing the real problem here is that the process crashed — the traceback shows an OSError about not being able to connect to huggingface.co to load files.
